summaryText:
Torren Wells joined Impact Church as a guest speaker and opened with the story of Copernicus, whose discovery that the earth is not the center of the universe was resisted by many. Pastor Torren used it to show that we still tend to place ourselves at the center. Following Jesus means putting Him on the throne of our hearts and recognizing that He, not we, is the center of our lives.

He then taught that God works through principles, patterns, and promises. Principles reveal God's nature, patterns reveal His ways, and promises reveal His faithfulness. He focused on one principle: God prepares, orders, and then fills. He pointed to creation, to Jesus preparing the room before raising a young girl, and to Jesus organizing the crowd before feeding them. His encouragement was that God wants to pour blessing, opportunity, and provision into our lives, and that putting our relationships, work, and finances in order with God first positions us to receive.

Pastor Torren said the Bible speaks often about money because money reveals what the heart values. Drawing on Matthew 6, he taught that we cannot serve both God and money, and that tithing is not only about stewardship but about lordship. He walked through three principles: the firstborn (Exodus 13, pointing to Jesus as the Lamb who redeems us), the first fruits (Cain and Abel in Genesis 4, bringing God our first and best), and the first tenth (Abram, Leviticus 27:30, Proverbs 3:9, and Malachi 3:10). He noted that Abram gave because he had already been blessed, not to earn a blessing.

He described tithing as a test we give God, not a test we must pass to earn favor. It is not a transaction but a response of trust and gratitude, and God uses it to shape our hearts. Using an illustration with two volunteers, he showed the difference between the bare minimum, generosity beyond it, and inconsistency. He shared how his father's example and his own decision to begin tithing at age 23 were about heart formation, not money. He encouraged the church to give through the church and to remember that God receives our giving as worship, moving from lifted hands to open hands.

The service closed with a prayer for generosity and a time to respond through giving. Pastor Torren also invited anyone who did not yet know Jesus to put their faith in Him, pointing to John 3:16 and leading a prayer of salvation, with many responding.
mainPoints: God works through principles, patterns, and promises, and He prepares, orders, and then fills, so putting our lives in order with God first positions us to receive His blessing.
Tithing is about lordship, not just stewardship: the principles of the firstborn, the first fruits, and the first tenth call us to give God our first and best because Jesus is preeminent.
Tithing is not a transaction to earn blessing but a response of trust to what God has already given, and it shapes our hearts toward generosity that goes beyond the bare minimum.

Monday.scripture: Matthew 6:33 (NIV): "But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well."
Monday.focus: Putting God at the center of your life instead of yourself.
Monday.action: Write down your top three priorities for the week. Then spend ten quiet minutes in prayer and Scripture before the day begins, placing God first on the list.
Monday.prayer: Lord, I place You at the center of my life. Help me seek Your kingdom first and trust You with everything else. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Mark 6:39 (NIV): "Then Jesus directed them to have all the people sit down in groups on the green grass."
Tuesday.focus: God prepares and orders before He fills.
Tuesday.action: Choose one area that feels cluttered or chaotic, such as your schedule, your workspace, or your commitments. Take one small step today to bring order to it.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, show me where my life needs order. Prepare me and my home so that I am ready for what You want to give. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 6:24 (NIV): "No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money."
Wednesday.focus: Lordship: asking what competes with God for your trust.
Wednesday.action: Take five minutes to list the things you depend on for security, such as money, status, or approval. Tell God honestly which ones you need to release to Him.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, You are Lord over all of my life. Search my heart and free me from anything that tries to take Your place. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Proverbs 3:9 (NIV): "Honor the LORD with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops;"
Thursday.focus: Giving God the first and the best.
Thursday.action: Look over your budget and make sure your giving to the local church is planned as the first line item. If you are not yet giving, prayerfully decide on one step of obedience you can take this week.
Thursday.prayer: God, everything I have comes from You. Teach me to honor You with the first and best of what You have given me. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Malachi 3:10 (NIV): "Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house."
Friday.focus: Giving as a response of trust, not a transaction.
Friday.action: Write down five ways God has already blessed you. Then pray over your giving, thanking Him for His provision and asking Him to shape your heart rather than only your habits.
Friday.prayer: Lord, thank You for the blessings You have already given. Help me give from trust and gratitude, not to get something in return. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: John 3:16 (NIV): "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."
Saturday.focus: Generosity that reflects the greatest gift ever given.
Saturday.action: Do one generous thing beyond the bare minimum today. Encourage someone with a kind note, give your time to help a neighbor, or share this sermon with a friend who could use encouragement.
Saturday.prayer: Father, thank You for giving Your Son. Make me generous with my heart, my time, and my resources so that others see Your love through me. Amen.

title: What the Bible Really Says About Tithing | Tauren Wells
